# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 39 CAPTAIN SAUL CROSSES THE BAR

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

Toward the end of September, the arrival of Adrian Treleaven’s book finally occurred one day. For a month, expecting its delivery, Captain Saul had reliably visited the Glen post office daily. Having refrained from going on this particular day, he received his copy from Lorna, who carried it home along with the ones belonging to her and Nell.
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0000 }

“This evening, we will bring it down to him,” Nell said, displaying the excitement of a schoolgirl.
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0001 }

Traversing the red road by the harbor during that bright, enchanting dusk made the extended trek toward the Point extremely enjoyable. Subsequently, the sun sank past the hills in the west into a valley likely overflowing with vanished twilights, and right at that moment, the giant light beamed from the point's white tower.
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0002 }

“By even the tiniest fraction of a second, Captain Saul is never late,” Lorna declared.
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0003 }

The expression on Captain Saul’s face as they presented him with the volume—HIS volume, changed and exalted—was something that neither Nell nor Lorna ever erased from memory. Those cheeks, recently drained of color, abruptly burned with a youthful flush; his eyes shone with the full intensity of his younger days; yet a quiver ran through his hands while he unclasped it.
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0004 }

Its title was merely The Life-Book of Captain Saul, and the title page displayed the names of Adrian Treleaven and James Garrick as joint authors. A photograph of Captain Saul himself served as the frontispiece, capturing him as he stood in the lighthouse doorway, gazing over the gulf. Adrian Treleaven had “snapped” this shot of him on a certain day during the writing of the book. Although Captain Saul was aware of this, he was unaware that the photograph would be included in the volume.
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0005 }

“Merely consider it,” he remarked, “that aged mariner situated right in an actual published volume. Today is the most triumphant day I have ever experienced. I feel as though I might burst, girls. Slumber will not come to me this evening. I shall peruse my tome entirely before the sun rises.”
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0006 }

“We will depart immediately so you can start,” Nell stated.
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0007 }

Captain Saul, who had been touching the volume with a sort of respectful ecstasy, then shut it firmly and set it to one side.
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0008 }

“No, no, you are not leaving until you have a cup of tea with the old man,” he objected. “I couldn’t allow that—could you, Matey? The life-book can wait, I suppose. I’ve been waiting for it for many a year. I am able to wait a bit longer while I am having a good time with my friends.”
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0009 }

Captain Saul busied himself with putting his kettle on the stove to boil, along with laying out his bread and butter. Although he was excited, he lacked his former brisk pace while moving. Slow and halting were his actions. Nevertheless, the girls refrained from offering assistance to him. They were aware that doing so would injure his feelings.
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0010 }

“You happened to choose the correct night for coming to see me,” he stated, pulling a cake out of his cupboard. “The mother of Leetle Joe dispatched a large basket packed with pies and cakes down to me this very day. May every skilled cook be blessed, I declare. Observe this fine cake, covered entirely in nuts and icing. It is not frequently that I am able to provide entertainment with this level of class. Sit down, girls, sit down! We will 'tak a cup o’ kindness yet for auld lang syne.’”
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0011 }

The girls commenced their enjoyment with great cheer. The tea equaled the finest ever prepared by Captain Saul. The cake from Little Joe’s mother represented the ultimate standard of cakes; Captain Saul proved to be the most charming of welcoming hosts, not once allowing his gaze to drift toward the corner where the life-book rested, fully adorned in its bold green and gold. Nevertheless, as his door ultimately shut behind Nell and Lorna, they were certain that he proceeded directly to it, and while traveling home they envisioned the joy of the elderly man absorbed in reading the published sheets in which his very existence was depicted with all the fascination and vividness of actual life.
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0012 }

“I am curious about his reaction to the conclusion—the conclusion that I proposed,” Lorna remarked.
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0013 }

It was something she would never discover. At an early hour the following morning, Nell woke up and saw Hugh leaning above her, completely clothed, his face showing a look of worry.
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0014 }

“Have you been summoned?” she inquired sleepily.
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0015 }

“No, Nell, I fear that a problem exists at the Point. The light continues to burn, even though sunrise occurred an hour ago. You are aware that Captain Saul has perpetually taken pride in lighting it precisely at sunset and extinguishing it precisely at sunrise.”
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0016 }

With a feeling of dismay, Nell sat up. She looked through her window to see the palely blinking light set against the blue skies of dawn.
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0017 }

“He might have dozed off while reading his life-book,” she remarked with concern, “or gotten so carried away by it that the light slipped his mind.”
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0018 }

A shake of his head came from Hugh.
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0019 }

“Captain Saul would not act in such a manner. Regardless, I am descending to check.”
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0020 }

“Hold on a moment so I can accompany you,” cried Nell. “Oh, indeed, I have to—Little Kit is going to rest for another hour, and I will summon Tabitha. Should Captain Saul be sick, a woman’s assistance might be required.”
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0021 }

An exquisite morning unfolded, brimming with hues and noises that were simultaneously mature and refined. Sparkled and dimpled like a young woman did the harbor; over the dunes, white gulls soared; a gleaming, marvelous ocean lay past the bar. In that initial, exquisite, unblemished light, the lengthy fields beside the coast were fresh and covered in dew. Up the channel, the wind arrived dancing and whistling, substituting the lovely quiet with a sound even more lovely. That early walk would have brought joy to Nell and Hugh, were it not for the ominous star upon the white tower. Fear, however, made them walk quietly.
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0022 }

No answer came to their knock. The door was opened by Hugh, and the two of them entered.
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0023 }

A deep silence filled the aged chamber. Upon the table lay what remained of the modest supper. Resting on the corner stand, the lamp continued to shine. Within a patch of sunlight beside the sofa, the First Mate slept.
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0024 }

Captain Saul was reclining upon the couch, his hands joined together across the life-book, which rested upon his chest opened to its final page. His eyelids were shut, and his countenance bore an expression of absolute serenity and joy—the expression belonging to a person who, after a length of searching, has finally discovered what was sought.
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0025 }

“Is he sleeping?” asked Nell in a trembling whisper.
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0026 }

Hugh walked over to the couch and leaned over his form briefly. Afterwards, he stood up straight.
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0027 }

“Yes, he is sleeping—well,” he stated softly. “Nell, Captain Saul has passed away.”
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0028 }

Although the exact time of his death was impossible for them to determine, Nell held to the belief that his desire was granted, causing him to depart as dawn arrived over the gulf. His soul floated away on that luminous current, crossing a morning ocean of silver and pearl toward the harbor outside the reaches of tempests and quiet waters where lost Margaret was waiting.
{: #nw-v04-c39-p0029 }
